topic: Thermodynamic Entropy and the Irreversibility of Time

partition_y.derived: scroll_progress × canvas_height — the height of the central dividing wall

particles.value: 150 red particles (left side) + 150 blue particles (right side), each with random velocities
particles.derived_update: bounce off canvas edges; bounce off wall if above partition_y

entropy_S.derived: fraction of red particles that have crossed to the right side (or blue to left) × 100

srtc.R: A dark split-canvas with 300 bouncing particles (red on left, blue on right). A central vertical wall separates the two halves—but only from partition_y downward. A red entropy counter (S = ...) updates live. A scroll track on the left fills red proportional to scroll_progress.
srtc.T: Scrolling the mouse wheel inside the widget increases scroll_progress, which raises partition_y (shortens the wall from the top), allowing particles to mix across the boundary. Scrolling back down lowers partition_y, re-blocking the passage.
srtc.C: As the wall is removed (scroll_progress → 1), particles irreversibly mix—entropy S increases monotonically. The constraint ΔS ≥ 0 maps directly to the unidirectional scroll interaction, visualizing time's arrow.
